title: An ingest that meets a store busy past its five-second wait is told to fix artefacts
body:
## What happens

Since issue 0420 (3d3441b10) every store transaction opens IMMEDIATE with a 5000 ms busy timeout, so a write waits for the writer lock rather than being refused at once. A lock held past that wait still reaches intentd's ingest as `database is locked`, wrapped as `FacadeError::Ingest` ("could not read the committed canon"). That variant's remedy is "fix the artefacts named above, then retry -- run `intent doctor` to list them" (`native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/src/facade.rs:2297`), which promises the wrong thing when the cause is a busy store: nothing is damaged and doctor has nothing to list. intentd.err.log showed that remedy on `database is locked` refusals on 2026-09-16 (16:46:51Z, 16:53:18Z, 16:55:02Z), from before 0420, read behind issue 0434.

## The fix

`FacadeError::Ingest` delegates its remedy to a busy-store remedy when its cause is a store busy past the wait, as it already delegates for `IngestError::EventLogUnreadable`. Measured: the busy timeout and IMMEDIATE transactions (intentsvcs store.rs, `BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS` and the one transaction door) and the remedy text above. Not yet measured: whether `StoreError` already carries a remedy for a busy store to delegate to, or whether that remedy is written once in the store for this. One arm: an ingest that meets a lock held past the busy timeout renders the busy remedy and not the artefacts one.

## Scope

Low, size S at most, intentsvcs only. Ruled by vc on 2026-09-17 as its own issue after 0434, landing as a train of one.
